Never log into your bank, email, or social media account using the same credentials you use elsewhere. Most breaches start from phishing emails impersonating you or compromised data. Even dedicated apps should use two-factor authentication (2FA) to limit your exposure. If there’s a recovery link in a suspicious message, hover over it and confirm through your bank’s official app.

# Understanding Fire Extinguisher Classifications

There are five distinct types of fire extinguishers, and knowing which one you need depends on the premises.

**Class A** (pieces of wood or paper) is the most basic type. This operates on the principle that water may put out grease or oil fires. You should use it on only solid combustibles like wood, fabric, or some plastics.

**Class B** extinguisher uses an agent that destroys only the heat and chemical reaction itself. Electricity or electricity is common. A Class B extinguisher should never be used on grease fires.

**Class C** (blister/mask) is designed to control *intrinsically* flammable liquid (kerosene) fires without fluid leaking. It is required for trucks.

**Class D** (driver) suppresses fires regardless of circuit potential, and is only required for fuel-fed appliances and explosions.

**Class K** (fuel) involves pure liquid substances like gasoline. You must never operate this, regardless of if you know the fuel.

For any specific circumstance, check the extinguisher label; the application guide should specify the exact chemistry of the liquid used. Once you identify the nature of the fire ( Class A, B, C, D, K) you can trigger the correct compatible appliance.
